title_hi: Assam Researcher Features in Stanford University’s Top 2% Scientists List
title_en: Assam Researcher Features in Stanford University’s Top 2% Scientists List
content_hi: Dr Sagar Bhattarai, a researcher from Sipajhar in Assam’s Darrang district, has earned recognition after being included in the list of the world’s top two per cent of scientists published by the prestigious Stanford University in the United States. Currently working as a research scientist at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati, Dr Bhattarai has been researching renewable solar energy for several years. “Stanford University has published its 2026 list of the top 2% of scientists, and I feel fortunate to be included in it. I would like to thank my workplace, IIT Guwahati, and the people of Sipajhar for their constant support. The university publishes this list every year," Dr Bhattarai told Pratidin Time. “My research focuses on solar power, a field we have been working on for several years. The selection is based on various factors, including the number of research papers published, their citation index and the consistency of the research work. There is no application process for inclusion in the list. Stanford University evaluates researchers across different fields, including physics, chemistry and other disciplines, and publishes the list annually," he added. His inclusion in the prestigious list has brought recognition to his home village and the wider Sipajhar region. The achievement highlights his continued work in the field of solar energy, which plays an important role in developing cleaner and more sustainable sources of power. . title_hi: Senior Advocate Ashok Bhan Honoured for Professional Excellence, Calls for Upholding Judicial Independence
title_en: Senior Advocate Ashok Bhan Honoured for Professional Excellence, Calls for Upholding Judicial Independence
content_hi: Srinagar, Oct 9: Senior Advocate Ashok Bhan was honoured by the International Law Centre for his professional excellence and contribution to the legal fraternity. "I receive this honour from the International Law Centre with profound gratitude and humility. I accept it not as a personal distinction, but as a tribute to the legal fraternity—the quiet, steadfast force whose dedication keeps the pillars of our constitutional democracy standing. For more than four and a half decades, I have served this profession as a lifelong student: with diligence, with integrity and with an unwavering faith in constitutionalism," he said. Ashok Bhan said, "To the young lawyers gathered here, I say this: law is more than a profession; it is a solemn trust placed in your hands. It binds you to society, to the Constitution and to the cause of justice. A strong judicial system is the bedrock of democracy, and an independent judiciary is the shield that protects every citizen’s rights and liberties." He further added, "To the young members of the Bar: pursue excellence, but never purchase it at the cost of integrity. Deepen your knowledge with humility; let courage be guided by compassion. Read the Constitution not as a relic of the past, but as a living promise renewed in every generation. Defend the independence of the judiciary, uphold the highest standards of professional ethics and never allow ambition to eclipse your duty to justice." The Supreme Court of India stands at the heart of our constitutional order. It is entrusted with preserving equality, pluralism, diversity and the rule of law—values that give our Republic both its character and its conscience. As guardian of the Constitution and fundamental rights, it must ensure that constitutional values rise above power, prejudice and arbitrariness. In a nation woven from countless languages, faiths, cultures and histories, the judiciary must remain a vigilant guardian of equal citizenship, individual dignity, liberty, social harmony and justice for all. "The future of our judicial system rests as much upon the integrity, scholarship and courage of lawyers as upon the wisdom of judges. A fearless judiciary cannot endure without a fearless and responsible Bar. Let your advocacy become a bridge for those whose voices are unheard, a safeguard for those whose rights are threatened and a source of strength for public faith in justice. Serve the law with conviction, defend liberty without hesitation and help ensure that justice remains not a distant ideal, but a living right belonging to every citizen," Bhan said. . content_hi: Gold is trading around 4,196 after breaking above the H1 descending trendline and reclaiming the 4,180 area. Macro News Gold is gaining as the U.S. dollar weakens and Treasury yields ease, while softer oil prices reduce some inflation pressure. Markets currently see only around a 17% chance of an October Fed hike, keeping the near-term backdrop supportive for Gold. The simple read 4,180–4,185 is now the key retest zone. If buyers defend this area, Gold may continue toward 4,225–4,230, the major structure high and 1.618 target. Key price zones 4,180–4,185 — breakout retest 4,145–4,150 — Fibo + trendline support 4,225–4,230 — major structure high 4,300 — 1.618 extension Momentum has shifted bullish after the trendline break. I prefer waiting for the 4,18x retest before looking for continuation. Can 4,180 hold as the new support and send Gold toward 4,225? . News Wire 24 ki vishleshan team dwara.
